subject: Post-call: model fit + Redwood-verified benchmarks / next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@fintechco.com>, Devon Price <devon.price@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: model fit + Redwood-verified benchmarks / next steps

Jamie/Devon — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our discovery: 

- Goal: Replace legacy NLU microservice for transaction categorization and fraud-related QA with an LLM-powered reranking + deterministic post-filter. Primary constraints: p95 latency <= 120ms at 1.5k TPS sustained (regional), ingestion of short batches (avg seq len ~60 tokens), and strict PII handling.
- Recommended serving configuration: open-bert-xxl-quant (4-bit) for core reranking; fallback to open-bert-large for edge cases where recall matters. We recommended quantized variants because they maintain similar quality with ~2.5x throughput improvements in our profiles.
- Attachments & links: attached the Redwood-verified benchmark PDF (summary), and uploaded the prompt set we discussed (fintechco_prompt_set_v1.json). Full raw run data is at https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/fintechco-DEAL-4821.

Key Redwood-verified perf highlights (from our internal run on NVIDIA A100, small region footprint):
- open-bert-xxl-quant: sustained throughput (TPS): 1.8k avg; p50 latency: 38ms; p95 latency: 108ms; p99: 160ms (see notes on warmup and KV-cache behavior in the PDF).
- open-bert-large: sustained throughput (TPS): 750 avg; p50 latency: 62ms; p95 latency: 140ms.

Quality/regression note: we ran the fintechco_prompt_set_v1 (included) across the two variants. open-bert-xxl-quant showed a 1.7% delta in F1 on the categorization holdout compared to the FP16 baseline; our eval harness flags any >2.0% delta as a regression. We recommend a brief A/B rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated eval monitoring in Redwood Console to validate in-prod quality.

Next steps I propose:
1) You share the production traffic pattern (CSV or histogram) and any additional prompt/edge-case examples (Devon mentioned richer error cases).
2) We run a short Dedicated trial on a reserved pool for 72 hours using your sample traffic and the included prompt set (bench run + logs).
3) Schedule a follow-up to walk through the console metrics and agree on rollout cadence.

I've cc'd Marissa (customer success / deployment) and Vivek (inference engineering) to help scope the Dedicated trial and answer any technical or compliance questions.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez

Alex — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few quick clarifying questions before we hand sample traffic to you: 

1) The p95 numbers look good, but can you confirm whether the RTX numbers in the PDF were run with batching enabled? Our production traffic will come in small bursts (avg batch size 3).
2) On the quantized model: the 1.7% F1 delta — is that consistent across categories? We have a few low-support categories that are business-critical.
3) Security: can the Dedicated trial be run in our VPC / with audit-logging enabled? We need to show SOC 2 evidence to our InfoSec team.

Also, can we get a short example of the eval harness config you used (seed, random sampling, and the metric definitions)? That will help our ML team validate the results.

—Devon

Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit + Redwood-verified benchmarks / next steps

Hi Devon — great questions. I'll answer each and loop in Vivek for the infra bits.

1) Batching: the reported numbers for open-bert-xxl-quant were run with adaptive batching enabled (Redwood smart-batcher), average batch size ~4 for that run. With avg batch size 3 you should see very similar p95s; the smart-batcher picks up short tails effectively. We can run a dedicated 72-hour replay with your exact batch histogram (recommended).

2) Quality across categories: the 1.7% F1 delta is an overall holdout aggregate. We did a category-level breakdown in the attached PDF (page 6) — the low-support categories show slightly higher variance (up to ~3.4% delta) for a handful of classes. That's why we recommend A/B rollout and the Redwood eval monitors (we can set threshold alerts on per-category F1 and false-positive rate). If you prefer, we can also hold those low-support categories on the FP16 variant while the rest run on the quantized model.

3) Dedicated trial + security: yes, we can run the Dedicated trial inside your VPC and enable audit-logging and KMS integration. I'll coordinate with our security team; Vivek — can you confirm KMS/HSM and audit-log retention defaults for a trial profile?

Eval harness config (summary):
- seed: 42
- sampling: stratified by category with min 50 examples per category (where available)
- metrics: macro F1, micro F1, recall@top1, false-positive-rate
- rollout monitor: per-category F1 delta vs baseline; alert threshold 2.0%

Links:
- Public run summary: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/fintechco-DEAL-4821 (same as Alex's link)
- Eval harness snippet & prompt set (attached): fintechco_prompt_set_v1.json
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/4821

Next steps: if you can share the traffic histogram and the low-support category list, we'll schedule the replay run for next week and prepare an infra checklist for VPC/KMS onboarding.

Thanks — Marissa
